name: x86-vm
label: x86-vm
machine_label: a current x86 cloud VM, 16 vCPU (8 cores with SMT, one thread per core, siblings idle), spot, PMU on
note: The x86 comparison VM: 16 vCPU = 8 cores with SMT. Threads map to physical cores, as on the Arm VM (where a vCPU is a core): one CPU per core is listed and its sibling stays idle, so N threads use N cores on both VMs. CPU numbers assume CPUs 0-7 are one per core and 8-15 their siblings; the micro runner checks this with lscpu -p=CPU,CORE at the start and refuses otherwise (edit the lists then). Microbenchmarks: threads 1, 4 and 7 (top: one spare core), histogram workers 1 and 7; the involuntary-switch bound is frozen from the session's smoke. End to end only 1w and 4w fit (SUT 0-4 with the main thread on 4, client 5-6, origin 7, siblings idle); the 12-worker rung of the Arm VM has no x86 counterpart here. Perf through sudo, PMU standard; steal gated at 2%. Binaries in <root>/<commit>/<target>, pinned by sha256 in boxes/sha256/x86-vm.txt after the rebuild.
